title: Snapdragon or Exynos? New upgrade for Exynos Galaxy S27 could make this a tough choice
summary: The Exynos Galaxy S27 might not lag behind the Snapdragon variant when it comes to cellular performance and efficiency.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR A Korean outlet reports that Samsung will use an in-house M2700 modem in some Galaxy S27 models. This modem will apparently deliver better power efficiency and faster data speeds than the Exynos modem in some S26 models. It’s believed that some Galaxy S28 models could get an M2800 modem that’s even more efficient than the S27 modem. Samsung has long offered Exynos or Snapdragon chipsets in its flagship phones, with the former being paired with a Samsung modem. Now, a Korean publication has encouraging news if you’re worried about efficiency and data speeds on the Galaxy S27 series . The Elec reports (h/t: SamMobile ) that Samsung will use a so-called M2700 modem in the Galaxy S27 series. This will ostensibly be restricted to the Exynos variants. The outlet claims that this is an external modem built on a 4nm manufacturing process, much like the Exynos Modem 5410 (also known as the Shannon 5410) seen in some Galaxy S26 series models.

title: I’ve used the Pixel 11 Pro XL and iPhone 18 Pro Max, and Apple’s ecosystem isn’t enough anymore
summary: Pixels have closed the gap.
body: Comparing the latest iPhone and Pixel devices used to be troublesome. It always boiled down to the same thing. Either you were firmly entrenched in the iOS ecosystem and were stuck with Apple, or you’d never use an iPhone, no matter how many advantages it had. Two distinct camps existed, with little hope of much crossover. It was rare for a buyer to sit down and decide between the two, but times have changed. Google worked to make Pixels a more attractive alternative to the iPhone, from a sleeker design to more intuitive software, and the results have been positive. Meanwhile, Apple’s definitely come back to the pack, and what used to be an easy choice is anything but. I’ve used the iPhone 18 Pro Max and Pixel 11 Pro XL , and Apple’s ecosystem doesn’t have the hold it once did.

title: How I turned my Pixel into the Nest Hub Google never made
summary: I wish I'd saved myself the trouble.
body: Google’s smart speaker lineup is going through a rough patch. There has been no new smart display launched in over half a decade, and the only new device announced was the Home Speaker, which has nothing special about it except that it runs Gemini out of the box. And Gemini for Home isn’t something to gloat about. I’m particularly disadvantaged because neither Gemini for Home nor a single Google smart speaker is available in India, leaving the whole wide market for Amazon Alexa to capture. Since I have a bunch of smart home devices that play nicer with Google’s smart speakers and dearly wanted a new Assistant/Gemini-powered smart display, I decided to take things into my own hands. I repurposed my Pixel into an always-on, always-listening smart screen with all the smarts of Gemini. It sounded doable in theory — I thought, what could even go wrong?

title: This Ultra phone could destroy Samsung and Google with long-overdue zoom camera upgrade
summary: Could this be the ultimate telephoto camera in 2027?
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR The vivo X500 Ultra is reportedly being tested with a larger 200MP telephoto camera. This is said to be a 1/1.12-inch Samsung sensor, dwarfing the 200MP tele sensor used on previous vivo flagships. This means the vivo X500 Ultra could have the largest 200MP telephoto camera upon its release. The vivo X100 Ultra was the first phone with a 200MP telephoto camera , enabling great long-range zoom as a result. Vivo has subsequently used this 200MP sensor or variations thereof on almost every Pro and Ultra phone since then, but a new leak suggests a major upgrade is coming. Prolific leaker Digital Chat Station has claimed on Weibo that the rumored vivo X500 Ultra is being tested with a 200MP 1/1.12-inch telephoto camera. Check out the machine-translated screenshot below.

title: Google Chat’s latest feature could finally end the post-meeting confusion
summary: Your meeting's biggest takeaways now land right where your team chats.
body: TL;DR Google Chat is getting automatic AI-powered meeting recaps that summarize discussions, decisions, and assigned action items. Recaps appear directly in meeting chats, complete with links to Gemini notes, recordings, and transcripts, so participants can catch up without digging through files. The feature is rolling out gradually to eligible Google Workspace subscribers. There’s always that one meeting where everyone agrees on the next steps, only for half the team to forget who promised what by lunchtime. Then comes the frantic search through notes, recordings, and chat messages to piece everything together. Google wants to put an end to that familiar office headache with a new Google Chat feature that brings the important stuff straight into your conversations after a meeting. In a blog post , Google revealed that Chat will automatically post meeting recaps once a Google Meet call ends. The feature builds on Meet’s Gemini-powered “ Take notes for me ” tool, turning its AI-generated notes into a handy summary that everyone in the meeting conversation can reference.

title: After a few days with the Fitbit Edge, I think Google found the sweet spot
summary: Right in the middle.
body: 2026 has proven to be a really strong year for Google wearables. The $100 Fitbit Air is an excellent entry point into Google Health and a solid all-around fitness tracker for someone who doesn’t want the distractions and bulk of a smartwatch. For folks who do want a smartwatch, the Pixel Watch 5 is one of the best you can buy. But with a $399 starting price, it’s a lot more expensive, too. That’s what makes the new Fitbit Edge so compelling. At $180, it’s substantially cheaper than the Pixel Watch while still offering an interactive AMOLED display — something the Air lacks. But with fewer onboard apps, no speaker or microphone, and a really compact/lightweight design, it’s more approachable for people who don’t want the smartwatch life, but still want to check the time or see workout data on their wrist.

title: One of Samsung’s most popular phones is now getting stable One UI 9 with Android 17
summary: The Galaxy A36 5G joins the list of Samsung phones with stable One UI 9.
body: TL;DR Samsung has started rolling out the stable One UI 9 update for the Galaxy A36 5G in Europe. The update comes with the build number A366BXXUCDZIF and weighs in at 2.4GB. Samsung could start rolling out the update to more regions in the coming weeks. The Galaxy A36 5G might not be the best mid-range smartphone, but it’s still one of the most popular Samsung phones . That could be because of Samsung’s promise of six years of OS updates, and it seems the company is staying on track with that pledge ( unlike some other Android brands ). According to user reports on Reddit , Samsung has started rolling out the stable One UI 9 update for the Galaxy A36 5G outside of South Korea. The update, reportedly rolling out in Europe now, has the build number A366BXXUCDZIF and weighs around 2.4GB (via SammyGuru ). It also includes the September 2026 security patch.

title: Fed up with ads and bloatware on your smart TV? People are vibecoding ways to remove them
summary: But before you start, beware of the potential cons of trying to hack a TV, especially a new one.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Hundreds of smart TV owners are vibe-coding solutions to remove ads and bloatware from their Android TVs. People are also using Claude Code or ChatGPT Codex to develop custom home screens or rescue old resource-hogging hardware. While the steps are easy, you must exercise caution, especially as vibe-coded solutions aren’t always so high on security. Bloatware and ads have long been pressing issues with smart TVs, and the problem has only gotten worse recently . Proficient users have previously resorted to specialized debloat tools for Android TV or the simpler push-it-under-the-rug approach of using free Android TV launchers that hide all the unnecessary bits . Now, a new savior is in town, and it’s one we’ve seen debloat and resurrect old devices before: Claude Code. YouTuber Ansub Khan recently posted a video account of how they let Claude completely reform their Android TV, removing unwanted ads and bloatware, and consequently making it work faster. The AI companion essentially built a new home screen experience from the ground up, so they see a clean and fresh UI, rather than what we’re accustomed to.

title: Google TV’s latest surprise is a collection of features you’ve probably seen
summary: The latest fullscreen announcement has a surprisingly long memory.
body: TL;DR Google TV is displaying a new fullscreen roundup highlighting six features and improvements. Most of the highlighted features have been available for months, with one dating back to last year. The roundup is appearing on Google TV Streamer and other Google TV devices, helping users discover features they may have missed. Turning on your TV sometimes comes with a surprise, whether it’s a redesigned home screen or a new feature waiting to be explored. Google TV is now greeting some users with a fullscreen announcement highlighting its latest improvements. There’s just one catch: Most of these features aren’t particularly new, and some have been around for nearly a year. As 9to5Google spotted, Google TV has started showing an October 2026 feature roundup on the Google TV Streamer and other supported devices. The screen highlights six additions, from free entertainment to new ways to enjoy your photos.

title: Some Google Home Speakers are downloading hundreds of gigs of data for no reason
summary: You may want to check how much data your Google Home Speaker is downloading.
body: TL;DR According to user reports, Google Home Speakers are downloading hundreds of gigabytes of data for no reason. Some users have shared screenshots showing their speakers downloading over 3TB of data in 30 days. Google has reportedly acknowledged the issue and has said that a fix is already rolling out. Smart speakers keep themselves updated by automatically downloading firmware updates in the background. However, this ability to quietly download data in the background can also become a problem, as we’re now seeing with the new Google Home Speakers . According to several users on Reddit, the new Google Home speaker has been absolutely hogging data in the background. Some users say their speakers downloaded nearly 140GB of data overnight, with no clear reason for it. Another user shared a screenshot of their internet statistics showing that their three new Google Home speakers downloaded around 280GB of data (see the first image below).

title: Googlebook owners finally get an explanation for the missing Find Hub app
summary: Google says laptop tracking needs a different approach, but what's next?
body: TL;DR Google has explained why it removed Find Hub support from first-generation Googlebooks, citing differences between how phones and laptops handle device tracking. The company says the Android app isn’t optimized for tracking laptops, especially when they’re closed and asleep. Googlebook owners can still use the Find Hub website to locate other devices, but Google hasn’t clarified whether their laptops can be tracked or if a replacement is coming. Googlebooks have had their share of early software frustrations , but the recent removal of Find Hub support raised a particularly uncomfortable question. How do you find your expensive new laptop if it goes missing? Google initially offered no explanation for the decision, leaving owners wondering whether the feature was broken or being abandoned. We’ve now heard back from the company, and its explanation sheds some light on what happened. In a statement to Android Authority , Google explained that Find Hub was primarily designed for mobile devices, which have different tracking requirements than laptops:

title: 82WORLD: LA Best Moments: ATEEZ Brings It Home, P1Harmony’s Big Tease and a BTS Throwback
summary: From P1Harmony and ATEEZ's headlining sets to intimate moments between artists and fans, here are the best moments from the first-ever 82WORLD festival.

The growing indie K-pop label’s inaugural 82WORLD: LA took over Los Angeles State Historic Park Oct. 17-18, drawing a reported 11,000 fans over two days. ATEEZ and P1Harmony headlined a lineup that also featured K-pop boy bands 8TURN, AMPERS&ONE and xikers , girl groups GIRLSET and cosmosy, J-pop sensations BE:FIRST, and a surprise addition of FiveALIVE. Sunday belonged entirely to ATEEZ and their fandom, ATINY, with the “ATEEZ x TINY Island” turning the park into a full day of ATZ programming that ended with a concert from the three-time Billboard 200 chart-toppers. But the performances were only part of the appeal. Between sets, fans played games like “This or That?” with their favorite acts, traded photocards with idols, and jumped into dance lessons, all while weaving between merch booths, photo ops and food trucks. It made for a weekend where artists and fans shared space far more often than at a typical festival or concert experience. Presented by Live Nation, the dates follow a run of European shows throughout late 2026 and arrive after the release of Same Difference , Swae Lee’s first full-length solo studio album, feauturing Post Malone, Jhené Aiko and French Montana among its collaborators. title: Google is giving you more creative control over Gemini Notebook’s video overviews and slides
summary: Google will soon roll out "co-creation" capabilities for two of Gemini Notebook's most popular features.
body: Credit: Karandeep Singh / Android Authority TL;DR Gemini Notebook is giving users more creative control over Slide Decks and Video Overviews through a feature called “Co-creation.” The platform will now walk the user through the creation flow, allowing them to steer the format and visual style before the final output. Co-creation capabilities will roll out to all users over the upcoming week. Gemini Notebook is a helpful tool for digesting large amounts of information. One way this is done is by breaking down your material into structured formats such as Audio Overviews and Study Aids, like flashcards. After a new update, you’ll soon have more creative control over the output from two of these formats. In a blog post , Google announced that it will add “co-creation” capabilities to Video Overviews and Slide Decks. Normally, Gemini Notebook will take a prompt and jump right to the final product. However, with co-creation, Notebook will walk you through the creation flow before outputting a result.

title: TP-Link signs deal to produce Wi-Fi 8 routers in US amid FCC ban
summary: Starting early next year, Wi-Fi 8 routers will be assembled by Key Tronic in Mississippi.
body: TL;DR TP-Link signs letter of intent with Key Tronic to build Wi-Fi 8 routers in Mississippi. Manufacture will begin early next year. TP-Link continues to pursue exemption from FCC ban while it faces lawsuits. The impact of the ban on foreign-made routers that the FCC implemented in March is still causing reverberations. While some router manufacturers have received exemptions , one of the largest, TP-Link is not among them. Now the company looks like it might have found a way to keep selling routers in the United States. TP-Link has announced a partnership with tech manufacturer Key Tronic Corporation to assemble its products in the United States, beginning with production of its Wi-Fi 8 routers in Mississippi (via PCMag ). Production will begin “as early as next year.”

One of Garmin’s biggest selling points is battery life, with many of its watches lasting well over a week between charges. That’s part of what made the company’s recent feature drop so appealing. It introduced all-day fall detection, new running tools, and hands-free voice commands using the “OK Garmin” hotword. Unfortunately, that last addition is now giving some owners an unpleasant surprise, with battery life estimates dropping dramatically after enabling it. summary: Apple's fall hardware blitz continues with MacBook and iPad reveals on October 28.
body: TL;DR Apple’s been rumored to be planning another fall hardware event, this one introducing the latest MacBook Pro and iPad models. The company has now confirmed its plans by sending out invites to an October 28 launch. In addition to a touchscreen MacBook Pro, we’re anticipating an OLED iPad Mini and M6 iPad. This fall has been all gas, no brakes for Apple. The company started off strong with the introduction of its iPhone 18 Pro lineup and its first-ever foldable model, the iPhone Duo . Then just last week we got to meet Apple’s new smart home lineup, including the HomeView display and a whole family of Apple Home connected devices . But we’ve also had one more big Apple launch event on our radar, after hearing plans about possible laptop and tablet news. And now, the invites are finally going out. While that earlier report pointed to October 27 as the likely date, we can now confirm that Apple’s instead planning to unveil its new hardware on October 28, according to invitations shared by the likes of Marques Brownlee over on X.

title: This magnetic accessory brings true flash back to phones
summary: The $85 accessory is iPhone-only for now, but Godox says Android support is coming.
body: TL;DR The $85 Godox A2 brings real xenon flash to smartphones. It’s iPhone-only for now, but the company says Android support is “under development.” Android devices led the way with built-in xenon flash, but abandoned the idea over a decade ago. For as outdated as it is, the image of a flashbulb going off as a button is pressed is one of the most universally recognizable signs of a photo being taken. And yet, our phones, which capture the majority of our photos , use LED flashes that don’t produce the same blinding intensity of light (or image quality) that are the result of “real” flash. But they can with the just introduced Godox A2, an accessory that uses a xenon flash tube and magnetically attaches to phones. The Godox A2 sells for $85, but don’t expect to order one for your Android device in the near future (via The Verge ). It’s iPhone-only for now, though on the product page, the company says that Android support is “under development.” Because the Godox A2 relies on a magnetic connection, like Apple’s MagSafe, it won’t work with every Android device. Right now that means Android phones with native support, like Pixel models since the 10 series or the Motorola Edge 70 Max …

title: Google Play Store bug is causing Collections confusion
summary: Is your Play Store Collections shortcut icon missing? You’re not alone.
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR A visual glitch is affecting the Play Store’s Collections shortcut on the stock Pixel Launcher. Users are reporting that the icon next to the Collections shortcut is completely blank. Google’s Pixel product support team recommends checking for updates, clearing the Pixel Launcher cache, or rebooting into safe mode to see if a third-party app is the issue. It has been about two years since Google introduced the Play Store feature known as “ Collections .” This feature organizes your apps by topic and highlights content recommended by your apps. It’s meant to help you discover new content or resume content already in progress right from your home screen. If you tried to set up the widget recently, you may have noticed that something is a little off. Accessing Collections is as easy as long-pressing on the Play Store app. It appears as the last option in the pop-up menu. Screenshots aren’t feasible with these dynamic QR codes, so subscribers are sidestepping the check by screen-sharing across multiple devices. Spotify is stepping up enforcement of its household location rules, leaving several Premium Family plan subscribers suddenly booted off their shared plans. The streaming giant is cracking down on family plan sharing to ensure that all members reside at the same location as the plan manager. A growing number of Reddit users are reporting that Spotify Family plan account holders are receiving sudden address re-verification prompts, particularly if they are not at the same location as other users on the Family plan. title: Hate the idea of paying for YouTube Premium? Imagine paying $240 a year for regular YouTube

If implemented, the change could require households to pay a license fee even to watch regular YouTube videos, without getting any Premium benefits. The proposal aims to address declining BBC funding but hasn’t been finalized. Does nothing sound worse than the idea of paying for YouTube Premium ? Well, imagine having to pay the government just for getting access to regular YouTube with none of the Premium perks attached. Sounds ridiculous, right? Unfortunately, that’s a possibility under consideration in the UK. To truly understand the development, you first need to understand the concept of a TV license fee in the UK. By law, you must have a TV license (£180 per year/~$240) if you plan on watching or recording programs as they’re being shown on live TV. You also need a license if you plan on watching or streaming programs live on online TV services, including the likes of YouTube, Netflix, and even Amazon Prime Video.
